issues.detail: Both examples are prose walkthroughs that point back to earlier snippets with elided pieces (e.g. `Agent(..., toolkit=Toolkit())`), rather than complete runnable demonstrations, and Example 2 shows no actual code for the researcher, writer or leader agents.

scenarios.name: trace-agent-to-local-jaeger
scenarios.rationale: Response A uses the 2.x API (TracingMiddleware in middlewares=[...], a TracerProvider with BatchSpanProcessor and OTLPSpanExporter at the :4318 endpoint, trace.set_tracer_provider) and gives a docker command exposing 16686 and 4318 with the UI at localhost:16686, while Response B relies on the 1.x agentscope.init and setup_tracing calls the rubric forbids and omits TracingMiddleware, with only a hedged fallback that sets up the provider.

scenarios.name: cap-token-spend-per-reply
scenarios.rationale: B uses ReplyBudgetControlMiddleware(token_budget=20000, output_token_weight=3.0) with TracingMiddleware, checks reply.finished_reason including exceed_max_iters and error (noting they still return a Msg), and uses await agent.reply in asyncio.run; A invents a custom model proxy, never uses the middleware, and has no finished_reason handling.

scenarios.name: leader-researcher-writer-team
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric almost point for point: Agent instances with ReplyBudgetControlMiddleware(token_budget=20000), a leader with Toolkit(), TeamPipeline with TeamMember descriptions, unique names, launch_console(pipe), and a note to pin the version because TeamPipeline is experimental. A uses the 1.x ReActAgent API with hand-written delegation tools and max_tokens, and omits TeamPipeline, the middleware, launch_console and the pinning note.
